pr.title: Keep the Codex rules to the bare project command
pr.head: d635238de2311ec099ec30014c16fa1499f5ad95

summary: project init writes two sets of permission rules into the person's own settings: allow rules for Claude Code in ~/.claude/settings.json, and allow rules for Codex in ~/.codex/rules/projector.rules. Codex runs a command that an allow rule matches outside its sandbox and without asking, so the rules have to match only Projector's own project command.

They matched more than that. When Codex sees a command that starts with a path to a program, such as /tmp/x/project summary publish or ./project list, it matches the rules written for the program's basename, project, unless a host_executable entry lists the paths it accepts. Projector's rules had no such entry, so any program named project, one an agent wrote into a temporary directory included, ran unsandboxed and unasked.

This change ends the generated rules file with host_executable(name = "project", paths = []). An empty list accepts no path, so a path to a project program goes to Codex's usual approval, while the bare project that every skill runs stays allowed. Claude Code needs no change, because it matches the command text, and Bash(project *) never matched a path.

A Codex that cannot parse host_executable falls back to an empty policy, which drops the person's own rules as well as Projector's. So the change also states a minimum Codex version in the README and in the init documentation.

cards.title: What Codex decides under each rules file
cards.html:
CommandBeforeAfter
project summary publishallowallow
/tmp/x/project summary publishallowusual approval
/usr/local/bin/project list --jsonallowusual approval
./project review publish 12allowusual approval

Checked with Codex 0.169 and codex execpolicy check --resolve-host-executables, which resolves paths as a live session does.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Rules file. A Starlark file in Codex's rules directory. Codex loads every .rules file there when a session starts.
  • prefix_rule. A rule that matches a command whose first words equal its pattern.
  • host_executable. An entry that lists which absolute paths to a program may match the rules written for its bare name.
  • Usual approval. What Codex does with a command no rule allows: run it in the sandbox, or ask, by the session's approval setting.

groups.title: The generated Codex rules
groups.kicker: The line that keeps the allow rules to the bare name
intro: CODEX_RULES is the whole text init writes to projector.rules. It now ends with CODEX_HOST_EXECUTABLE, the host_executable entry with an empty list of paths. The hint init prints when it cannot write the file now names that line beside the prefix_rule entries, so a person who adds the rules by hand adds it too.

Because init compares the file whole, a file an earlier release wrote reads as out of date, and the next init at a terminal rewrites it. The permission-rules digest changes with the text, so sessions tell the person to run init again.

files.note: Adds CODEX_HOST_EXECUTABLE, appends it to CODEX_RULES, and names it in the hint for a kept file.

checks.text: With Codex 0.169, the base's rules allow /tmp/x/project summary publish, /usr/local/bin/project list --json, ./project review publish 12, and x/project list, and the head's rules match none of them. The bare project summary publish is allowed under both.
Codex's rules loader falls back to an empty policy when a file fails to parse, and only logs a warning, as the comment and the documentation say. Read in Codex's own source.

init does not check the installed Codex's version before it writes this line. On a Codex too old to parse it, the person's own rules, forbidden ones included, stop applying with nothing on screen to say why. The review lists a version check as a suggestion.

Codex 0.107.0 is the first release whose rules parser registers host_executable, and 0.106.0 has no such builtin, so 0.110 is a stricter minimum than parsing needs. The review lists the correction as a suggestion.

groups.title: The permission tests
groups.kicker: Three path cases, checked against a real Codex where one is installed
intro: DECISIONS is the table of command lines with the decision each host must reach under Projector's rules. It gains three lines that start with a path to project, and each must reach no decision on either host. The test that runs the real codex CLI now passes --resolve-host-executables, so it resolves paths as a live session does. It is the test that catches the hole: against the base's rules it fails on exactly the three new lines.

checks.text: codex_decision, the test's own model of Codex, compares words and never resolves a path, so it reaches none for the path cases at the base too. Only the test that runs codex tells the two rules files apart, and it is skipped where Codex is not installed.

files.note: Adds the path cases to DECISIONS, resolves paths in the real Codex check, and checks that the documentation shows the host_executable line.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The rules block, the minimum Codex version, and the check command
intro: The init section of docs/cli.md shows the new last line of the rules file, says why it is there, and says what an older Codex does with it. Its example codex execpolicy check command gains --resolve-host-executables. The README's requirements name the minimum Codex version.
